plain.li: [skill:Melee] I'm the one who runs at them. Give me plates or thick leather and I'll keep doing it.
[!lowtech] A vest, a helmet, anything that has stopped a bullet before. My shirt never has.
[hurt] I'm still healing from the last fight. I'd rather the next one hit armor first.
[old] I've fought for this colony longer than most. These old bones would like some armor over them.

warm.li: I'll keep going out first when they come. I'd just like to be harder to hurt when I do.
[trait:Kind] If I'm wearing armor, the others won't have to carry me back inside. That's half of why I'm asking.
[afterraid] I watched the others patching each other up after that raid. Armor would mean less of that next time.

blunt.li: Armor. Before they come back.
[trigger:raid] They nearly had me today. Make me armor that stops a blade.
I'm not facing the next raid in a shirt.
[trait:Bloodlust] I like being in the thick of it, and I'd like to stay there longer.

cheerful.li: Armor with straps that actually fit! I'd polish it every evening.
[skill:Melee] Put me in armor and I'll be first through the gap every time.
[trigger:raid] Still in one piece after that one! Some armor would help me stay that way.

gloomy.li: I keep thinking about where the last one would have hit me. Armor would let me stop.
[night] Every night I count my bruises from the last fight. With armor there'd be fewer to count.
[trigger:raid] They came close today. Next time it won't be close.
Somebody has to stand at the front. It's usually me, and I usually have nothing on but a shirt.

cold.li: Armor costs less than a funeral, and far less than finding another fighter.
[trigger:raid] I counted the hits I took today. Every one of them would have stopped at a plate.
[skill:Shooting] I aim better when I'm not worried about being hit. Armor takes care of the worry.

plain.li: [trigger:raid] When they come back, I'll be wearing this. Thank you.
Took me a while to get the straps right. It fits now.

warm.li: I'll look after it, and it'll look after me. Thank you.

blunt.li: Good. Let them try now.

cheerful.li: I've worn it all day, even to supper!

gloomy.li: I'll be as scared as ever next time, only better covered.

cold.li: Noted. I'll fight further forward now.

plain.li: [afterraid] Still in the shirt I wore for the last raid, holes and all.

warm.li: I'll stand in front anyway. Someone has to.
[trait:Kind] I'll go out as I am. Just have someone ready with bandages.

cheerful.li: No armor? Then I'll just have to be very quick on my feet!

plain.li: Still going into every fight in a shirt. About that armor.
[trigger:raid] They'll be back, and I'm still in the same shirt.

warm.li: Whenever there's a free day at the bench, I'd still be glad of that armor.

blunt.li: Armor. Still waiting.

cheerful.li: My shirt has lived through two fights now! I wouldn't ask it to live through a third.

gloomy.li: Another day closer to the next raid, and nothing between me and it.

cold.li: I'm still unarmored. The raiders won't wait for the council.

warm.li: [grieving] Some of us need somewhere to set our grief down for a while. A shrine would be that place.
I'd sweep it every morning and leave it open for whoever needs it.
[petition] It isn't only me. A few of us have been praying in corners for a while now.
[old] I've knelt on a lot of cold floors in my life. I'd like one place that was made for it.

blunt.li: Build {THING}. I'll pray for whoever does the work.
[afterraid] We were lucky in that raid. I'm not pushing that luck without giving thanks somewhere.
I've been praying next to the woodpile. It isn't fit, and you know it.

cheerful.li: I've already picked out the stones for {THING}! They look very holy, for stones.
[spring] Everything's coming up green! Let's give thanks somewhere nice.
A shrine with candles all around it, and fresh flowers when there are any!

gloomy.li: I pray every night and nothing answers. Maybe a proper altar would get their attention.
[night] The nights are long out here. I'd like somewhere to spend some of them besides my bed.
[grieving] I talk to the dead now. I'd like a better place for it than the back of the storeroom.

cold.li: People who pray hold up better under pressure. Build {THING} and watch.
[afterraid] Several of us prayed through that raid, behind crates and under tables. Give it a proper place.
I keep my faith to myself. I'd like somewhere to keep it, too.

plain.li: [grieving] I went and said their name there this morning, as loud as I liked.

warm.li: I've set a candle there for anyone who wants one lit.

blunt.li: Good. Now leave me be while I use it.
It'll do. It'll more than do.

cheerful.li: It's even nicer than the one I drew in the dirt!

gloomy.li: Still no answer. But it's quieter there than anywhere else here.

cold.li: It will do. Don't follow me there.

plain.li: [night] I'll pray in bed, then, with the blanket over my head.

gloomy.li: [grieving] I'll keep talking to them from behind the storeroom, then.

cold.li: Then I'll keep my faith where none of you can see it.

plain.li: [night] Prayed behind the storeroom again last night, by moonlight.

cold.li: My prayers are still said behind the storeroom. I haven't stopped noticing.

warm.li: [winter] It's a long, cold walk at night for the older ones. {THING} closer in would be a kindness.
I'd help dig it and I'd help keep it clean. We only need {THING}.
[large] With this many of us, a proper latrine would spare a lot of awkward mornings.

blunt.li: [trigger:outside] I'm not squatting behind the woodpile again. Build {THING}.
Everything else here has four walls. Give this four walls.
[rain] Wet feet, wet knees, wet everything. Build {THING}.

cheerful.li: A seat and a door that shuts! I'd never be late for breakfast again.
[spring] The bushes are full of nettles again! I'd love {THING} before I find any more of them.
I'll make a sign for the door myself, if we ever get {THING}.

gloomy.li: [night] I lie awake putting off the walk out to the trees. Then I have to go anyway.
Every morning starts with the same walk through the wet grass to the bushes.
[winter] Out in the snow again this morning, with the wind getting in where it shouldn't.

cold.li: A good part of our sickness starts where we relieve ourselves. Build {THING}, well away from the water.
[large] Too many of us using the same patch of ground. You'll smell the result before you see it.
Privacy costs the colony little and me a great deal. Build {THING}.

plain.li: No more walking out to the trees in the dark.

warm.li: [old] Thank you. My knees will be grateful every morning.

blunt.li: Good. Stay out of the woodpile, all of you.

cheerful.li: I've been three times today just to use the door!

gloomy.li: [winter] At least the snow can't get at me in there.

cold.li: Good. The water stays clean now.

plain.li: [winter] Out to the trees again, in the snow.

cold.li: Then the next sickness goes on the council's account.
Still no {THINGBARE}. The flies have noticed, even if the council hasn't.

warm.li: [evening] I'd like us all at one table for supper, even if it's a squeeze.
[newcomer] The new ones eat off their knees in the corner. Let's give them a chair at the table.
[old] My knees don't like eating standing up. A few more chairs and I could sit with the rest of you.

blunt.li: [eating] I'm eating this standing up. Again.
Count the people. Count the chairs. Then build the difference.
[trait:Abrasive] I don't even like most of you, and I still want a seat at the table.

cheerful.li: More chairs! Then we can all fight over the salt like a proper family.
[evening] Supper would be twice as loud with all of us at one table, and I'd love it.
[child] Can we have enough chairs so I can sit with everybody?

gloomy.li: [eating] I'm eating on the floor by the wall again. The food's no better down here.
[evening] By the time I get to supper, every seat is taken.
[winter] There's never a seat left, so I eat by the door, where the draft comes in.

cold.li: We lose part of every day to people waiting for a seat. More chairs fix that.
People who eat together argue less. Seat us all and I'll have less to listen to.
[large] There are more of us than chairs. That is an easy problem to solve.

plain.li: [evening] Supper tonight, and every one of us had a seat.

warm.li: [newcomer] I sat at the table tonight with everyone else. Thank you.

blunt.li: Good. Now pass the salt.

cheerful.li: I counted the chairs twice, and there's one for everybody!

gloomy.li: A chair of my own at supper. I'd forgotten what that was like.

cold.li: All of us fed at one sitting. That saves an hour a day.

plain.li: [evening] Supper standing up again, then.

cold.li: Then we keep eating in shifts and grumbling in shifts.

plain.li: [evening] Somebody ate supper on the doorstep again last night.

cold.li: There are still fewer chairs than mouths.

warm.li: I'd keep the water hot for whoever's next. We'd all be in better tempers for it.
[old] At my age a warm soak does more for me than any medicine.
[afterraid] After a day like that one, a hot bath would help more of us than you'd think.

blunt.li: [hot] My shirt is stuck to me. Build {THING}.
A bucket isn't a bath. Build a bath.
[skill:Mining] I come in from digging gray from head to foot, and a bucket doesn't touch it.

cheerful.li: Hot water up to my chin! I've been thinking about it all week.
[winter] A hot bath on a snowy evening! I can't think of anything better.
I'd sing in the bath, and you'd all be glad of the noise, I promise.

gloomy.li: [winter] My hands haven't been properly warm since autumn. A hot bath might change that.
I scrub and scrub out of that bucket, and I'm never clean.
[lowmood] Some days a long, hot bath is the only thing I can think of that might help.

cold.li: Clean people get sick less. A bath costs less than the medicine.
I don't enjoy smelling the rest of you. I assume you don't enjoy smelling me.
[hot] In this heat the smell at supper has become a health problem. Build {THING}.

plain.li: [winter] Hot water in the middle of winter. I stayed in until my fingers wrinkled.

warm.li: [old] My back hasn't felt this good in years. Thank you.

blunt.li: Took long enough. Don't use all the hot water.

cheerful.li: Two baths today, and I'm going back for a third!

gloomy.li: I'd forgotten what color my skin was under the dirt.

cold.li: Clean. I'll be using it every evening.

cheerful.li: No bath? I'll stand out in the next rainstorm with the soap!

cold.li: Then don't complain about the smell at supper.
Still washing out of a bucket. The smell hasn't improved.

blunt.li: [trigger:cold] I'm sleeping in my coat. Put {THING} in my room.
[repeat] I've asked about my room before. It's still no good at night.

gloomy.li: [trigger:heat] I lie on top of the blanket and wait for the room to cool off. It never does.
[trigger:cold] The cold gets into my room after dark and stays there until morning.

cold.li: [trigger:cold] Someone who sleeps cold works slowly. Fix my room and you fix the work.
[old,trigger:cold] At my age, a cold room is how people catch their death. I'd prefer not to.

warm.li: I slept the whole night through and woke up rested. Thank you.

gloomy.li: [trigger:heat] I slept. Not well, but I slept.

blunt.li: [trigger:heat] Fine. I'll sleep outside with the bugs.

cheerful.li: [trigger:cold] More blankets, then! I'll be the warmest heap in the colony.

cold.li: [trigger:heat] Then expect me slow and short-tempered until the weather turns.

warm.li: Whenever there's a free afternoon, my room still needs {THING}.

cold.li: My room is still wrong at night, and my work still shows it.
[trigger:barracks] In the barracks, the others know when I sleep and when I wake. I'd rather they didn't.

cheerful.li: I've already picked a corner for my own room! It only needs walls around it.

cold.li: [rich] The colony can afford it now. My room should show that it can.
My room is still bare. People notice, and so do I.

cheerful.li: I'll go and tell {OTHER_nameDef} whenever there's good news. There's a proper place for it now.

warm.li: [grieving] I'll keep {OTHER_nameDef}'s name, at least, and say it at supper.

cold.li: Then I'll stop counting on this place to look after its dead.

plain.li: [rain] {OTHER_nameDef} lay out in the rain again last night, so I'm asking again.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} deserves a sunny spot, and there are still plenty to choose from.

blunt.li: That'll do for a while. Don't waste it.

cheerful.li: Look at all of it! I could patch up a whole caravan.

gloomy.li: [trigger:raid] Enough for the next raid. Maybe not the one after.

plain.li: [lowtech] I'll go out and look for healroot myself, then.

cheerful.li: Then I'll just have to be very careful with what's left!

warm.li: [evening] We all stayed at the table long after the food was gone. Thank the cook for me.

cold.li: A proper meal. I can already think more clearly.
The meals are still poor. I'm still keeping track.

warm.li: I saw people laughing together tonight who don't usually say a word to each other. Thank you for that.

blunt.li: Good night. Same again next season.

gloomy.li: No party. Just another evening that ends early.

cold.li: No party. Then tempers keep building, and I'll keep my distance while they do.

warm.li: Thank you. I'll make sure it's never pointed anywhere but outward.

gloomy.li: A better {SUBJECT}. One less way to die out there.

warm.li: When someone has a free hour at the bench, I'd still be glad of a better {SUBJECT}.
Thank you for trusting me with {SUBJECT}. I'll make it worth it.

gloomy.li: Work I'm good at, for once. It helps more than I'd say.

cold.li: On {SUBJECT} at last. The work will improve, and quickly.
I'm still not on {SUBJECT}, and it's still being done worse than I'd do it.

warm.li: Everyone I care about, at one table, on my birthday. I couldn't ask for more.

blunt.li: Good food. Good birthday. Thanks.

gloomy.li: One more year, marked properly. That's more than I expected.

cold.li: My birthday is close. I've told the cook, in case the council forgets.

warm.li: The evenings are going to be so much better now. Come and play, all of you.

gloomy.li: A new way to pass the evenings. It'll keep my mind off things for a while.

cold.li: Good. Bored people make trouble, and now they have less reason to.
Still nothing new to do in the evenings. Tempers are getting shorter, and I'm counting.

warm.li: If we each take a corner after supper, the place would be clean in no time. I'll start with the worst one.
[trait:Kind] The sick and the little ones shouldn't be breathing in this dirt. Could we have a cleaning day?

blunt.li: Somebody pick up a broom. Anybody.
[rain] The mud's halfway up the walls now. Clean it.

cheerful.li: I've got a broom and a song for sweeping to! I only need a few more pairs of hands.
[spring] Spring cleaning! Let's throw the doors open and get into every corner.

gloomy.li: I sweep my bit, and the next day it's dirty again. I'd like the whole place clean, just once.
[afterraid] The floors still show where people were hurt in that raid. I'd rather not keep walking over it.

cold.li: Dirty floors slow the work and spoil the food. Clean them.
[large] The more of us there are, the faster this place gets filthy. It needs cleaners, not hope.

warm.li: It looks like a home again. Thank you, all of you.

blunt.li: Better. Now wipe your boots.

cheerful.li: You can see the floor! I'd forgotten what color it was.

gloomy.li: Clean, for now. I'll enjoy it while it lasts.

warm.li: I'll keep my own corner clean, at least.

blunt.li: Fine. Live in it.

gloomy.li: The dirt wins again.

warm.li: [trait:Kind] We'd all feel more like people with somewhere to wash. Even {THING} would do.
I'd keep it filled for everyone, if we had {THING}.

blunt.li: [hot] Three days in this heat and nowhere to wash. Build {THING}.
I'm not sleeping next to people who smell like this. Build {THING}.

cheerful.li: Clean hands at supper, imagine it! All we need is {THING}.
[spring] Everything else gets washed in the spring rain. I'd like a turn too!

gloomy.li: I've stopped trying to get clean. There's nothing to get clean with.
[winter] I'd wash, if there were anywhere to, but there isn't.

cold.li: [afterraid] Blood under the fingernails turns into a fever. Build {THING}.
Dirty hands carry sickness to the food. I'd like that stopped.
